# Cross-Exchange Liquidity Commentary – 29 July 2026

US equity markets command a decisive liquidity advantage, with Nasdaq 100 and NYSE delivering superior execution costs across all metrics: Nasdaq's 0.0025% per $1M traded ILLIQ and 0.7631% AR spread lead the field despite modest 1.2508% turnover, while NYSE's 0.6459% spread and 0.0060% per $1M ILLIQ reflect deep order books supporting $255.6M comparable volume. Tokyo Stock Exchange ranks third with strong 3.9703% turnover but trails materially on price-impact metrics at 0.0372% per $1M ILLIQ. The mid-tier European cohort—Euronext, SIX Swiss, and Xetra—clusters around 0.05–0.55% ILLIQ and 0.47–0.54% spreads with modest volumes, though Euronext's tighter 0.5145% spread masks weaker 0.0308% per $1M ILLIQ, suggesting concentrated order flow rather than deeper liquidity. Hong Kong and Korea Exchange occupy a transitional zone; Korea Exchange exhibits the ranking's widest structural deterioration with 0.1496% per $1M ILLIQ and 1.5269% spread despite respectable 1.5770% turnover, signaling persistent friction costs. London Stock Exchange anchors the bottom tier at 0.0828% per $1M ILLIQ and 0.7946% spread with only $10.6M turnover, reflecting post-settlement consolidation effects.
